correctness.rationale: At \(t=1\), the source recurrence gives \(m_1=(1-\beta_1)h x_1\), \(v_1=(1-\beta_2)h^2x_1^2\), and \(x_2=x_1[1-(1-\beta_1)h\widehat\eta_1]\). The raw rate ranges over all positive values as \(|x_1|\) varies, so its attainable supremum after clipping is exactly \(u_1\). Thus the sharp condition follows from \(|1-z|\le1\) iff \(0\le z\le2\). The unsafe neighborhood is obtained by solving the upper-clip inequality. The inspected verifier independently checks the recurrence, safe/unsafe sides and all stated default numbers. One nonessential sentence in RESULT.md says the clipped rate attains the entire closed interval even when \(\ell_1=0\); in that boundary case the attainable set is \((0,u_1]\), but the supremum and every theorem statement are unchanged.
residual_risks: The closed-interval attainability wording at \(\ell_1=0\) is slightly imprecise but does not enter the proof of the universal maximum condition.

value.rationale: AdaBound's defining mechanism is intended to suppress extreme adaptive rates. The theorem identifies an exact pointwise safety requirement on that upper bound, quantifies the source defaults on the canonical scalar-curvature test, and separates mere finiteness of a clipped rate from curvature-compatible descent. The narrow scope is mathematically motivated by the algorithm's central design feature rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.

final_claim: For source-form AdaBound on the deterministic scalar quadratic \(f(x)=h x^2/2\), universal first-step objective nonincrease over every nonzero initialization holds exactly when \((1-\beta_1)h u_1\le 2\); when it fails, a whole small-initialization neighborhood is clipped to \(u_1\) and has constant amplification \([1-(1-\beta_1)h u_1]^2>1\), yielding the stated exact frontier for the source-recommended schedule and defaults.
